Apple's new Upgrade Program has an important caveat: "If you're leasing an iPhone, you must connect to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when signing up."

John Gruber of Daring Fireball offers a possible explanation for this requirement in a new article today.

Apple Upgrade's iPhone Restriction

According to a former Apple employee who worked on Apple's carrier team and reached out to Gruber via email, the requirement stems primarily from agreements Apple has signed with US carriers Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

These agreements with each carrier are reportedly worth "hundreds of millions of dollars," and in exchange, Apple makes certain concessions. The requirement that iPhones purchased through Apple Upgrade must be connected to a T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T account appears to be one such concession.

The former Apple employee went on to detail how these agreements work:

There's also a fraud and risk assessment angle to this. A former Apple Store retail employee told Gruber that fraud cases involving iPhones have "dramatically increased" since Apple began offering carrier installment plans in its retail stores.

Apple does note that while you need to connect your iPhone to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when signing up for Apple Upgrade, the phone itself remains unlocked: "Leasing an iPhone requires selecting a qualifying carrier (but not a prepaid plan). Leased iPhones remain unlocked at all times, so you can switch carriers at any time, subject to the terms of your selected carrier."

You can read Gruber's full article over at Daring Fireball.
